findings.title: immediateDelete path does not clean up the database record
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` cancels the email in SendGrid but returns without deleting or updating the `workflowReminder` row in the database. The record remains with `scheduled: true` and no `cancelled` flag. In the reschedule flow (`handleNewBooking.ts` line 968), the old booking is not deleted—only marked cancelled—so this orphaned reminder row persists indefinitely until the CRON's `deleteMany` eventually removes it (only after `scheduledDate` passes). If the scheduled date is far in the future, this is a long-lived orphan record. The function should delete the row or set `cancelled: true` after the SendGrid cancel call.

findings.title: Async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called without await inside forEach
findings.body: The calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions invoked inside `forEach` without `await`. This means: (1) the HTTP response is returned before the database updates (setting `cancelled: true` or deleting SMS reminders) complete, so if the process is interrupted the cancellation may be lost; (2) any errors thrown become unhandled promise rejections rather than being caught. The same pattern appears in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` line 488 and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` lines 376, 519, 574. Use `for...of` with `await` or `Promise.all` with `.map()` to ensure the operations complete before proceeding.

findings.title: try-catch around forEach with async callbacks does not catch promise rejections
findings.body: In the reschedule path, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are async calls inside `forEach`, wrapped in a try-catch. However, `forEach` does not propagate rejected promises to the enclosing try-catch. If the SendGrid or Twilio API call fails, the error becomes an unhandled promise rejection and is never logged by `log.error`. The try-catch gives a false sense of safety. Replace with a `for...of` loop and `await`, or use `Promise.allSettled`.

findings.title: Single try-catch around entire cancellation loop causes partial processing on failure
findings.body: The SendGrid cancellation loop (lines 56-73) is wrapped in one try-catch. If the `client.request` call fails for one reminder (e.g., network timeout), the loop aborts and remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are not cancelled. They will be retried on the next CRON run, but if the failure is persistent (e.g., a malformed `referenceId`), all subsequent reminders in the batch are blocked. Move the try-catch inside the loop so each reminder is handled independently.

findings.title: Unscheduled reminders query does not exclude cancelled reminders
findings.body: The query for unscheduled reminders (line 80-98) filters on `scheduled: false` but does not exclude `cancelled: true`. Currently, `cancelled` is only set on reminders that already have a `referenceId` (i.e., `scheduled: true`), so this is safe today. However, if a future code path sets `cancelled: true` on an unscheduled reminder (or if data is manually edited), the CRON would schedule and send an email that should have been cancelled. Adding `cancelled: { not: true }` (or `OR: [{ cancelled: false }, { cancelled: null }]`) to the where clause would make this defensive.

findings.title: Async forEach with await inside callback does not sequence operations
findings.body: At line 574, `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` uses an async callback. The `forEach` method ignores the returned promise, so all iterations start concurrently and the outer function does not wait for them to finish. This means the workflow update response is sent before all reminders are cancelled. If a reminder cancellation fails, there is no error propagation. This is the same fire-and-forget pattern as in other files but is particularly notable here because new reminders are created immediately after (line 581+), potentially racing with the cancellations.
